drop.web-performance-sr4-11: weak_card: strawman (nobody expects client-rendered content before the JS runs), and the cited rendering-on-the-web page says nothing about LCP.
drop.web-performance-sr4-12: weak_card: truism with a hedge verb, and the words 'the TTFB portion of LCP' give away sr4-01.

drop.web-performance-sr7-11: weak_card: its premise ('while a script stalls the main parser') gave away sr7-06, and it overlaps with sr4-06 (preload scanner reads HTML only). The card that gave away is dropped, but r7 reaches 9 cards with the sr7-01 rewrite, so this one is dropped too.

drop.web-performance-sr10-01: weak_card: truism (nobody can find a URL inside a file before downloading it). The verifier's preload-ignores-unicode-range replacement would give away sr10-08 and sr10-10, so sr10-03 and sr10-09 are rewritten instead to keep r10 at 9 cards.
drop.web-performance-sr10-04: ambiguous: Chromium and Firefox treat auto like block, and web.dev calls block the default, so the card is false only through the word 'explicit'. The suggested inlined @font-face replacement rests on the same fact as sr10-08 (a font is requested only once the browser knows text needs it), so no clean card is possible. Dropped.
drop.web-performance-sr10-11: weak_card: a near-copy of MDN's opening definition of size-adjust. The suggested replacement is still definitional. r10 reaches 9 cards with the sr10-03 and sr10-09 rewrites.

web-performance-sr7-01.reason: weak_card (definition card). Rewriting is needed because dropping sr7-01, 02, 06 and 11 would leave r7 with 8 cards. The new card covers the section's untested fact that the CSSOM is not built incrementally. MDN: "The CSS object model gets built as the CSS is parsed, but can't be used to build the render tree until it is completely parsed" and "While the DOM construction is incremental, CSSOM is not." (final: keep)
web-performance-sr7-01.statement: The browser waits until a stylesheet is completely parsed before it uses that CSSOM to build the render tree.
web-performance-sr7-01.explanation: Later CSS rules can override earlier ones, so MDN says the CSSOM is used for the render tree only once fully parsed, while DOM construction is incremental.

web-performance-sr9-02.reason: ambiguous: Chrome renders layered progressive AVIF, so the AVIF fact is contested. Replaced with the stable progressive-rendering fact for JPEG (stays false). web.dev: baseline JPEGs "are rendered from top to bottom as the transfer progresses"; progressive: "The entire image appears immediately, albeit blurry, and grows clearer as the transfer continues." The statement says 'at full quality' because each progressive scan also runs top to bottom. (final: keep)
web-performance-sr9-02.statement: A progressive JPEG shows its top part at full quality before its lower part appears during download.
web-performance-sr9-02.explanation: That describes a baseline JPEG. A progressive JPEG shows the entire image at once, blurry at first, and each scan sharpens it as the transfer continues.
web-performance-sr9-02.misconception: Progressive loading means the image fills in from the top at full detail.

web-performance-sr10-03.reason: weak_card (the name 'swap' gives the answer away). Rewriting is needed because dropping r10's weak and ambiguous cards would leave 7 cards with 2 true. The new card is the verifier's replacement, reworded to avoid the hedge 'can'. CSS Fonts 4 on fallback: "if too much time passes, the fallback will be used for the rest of the page's lifetime instead." It is cited to the spec because MDN does not state the lifetime point. (final: fixed)
web-performance-sr10-03.statement: Under font-display: block, the browser shows fallback text if the web font is still loading after the block period.
web-performance-sr10-03.explanation: block gives a short block period and an infinite swap period: text stays invisible only briefly, then a fallback font shows it until the web font arrives and swaps in.

web-performance-sr10-09.reason: weak_card (advice to measure is never false). Rewritten as the second r10 true card that keeps the section at 9 cards and 4 true to 5 false. The new card uses the substantive fact on the same page: "confirm that your site uses a Content Delivery Network (CDN) and HTTP/2. Without use of these technologies, it's much less likely that self-hosted fonts deliver better performance", plus the Web Almanac finding. (final: fixed)
web-performance-sr10-09.statement: web.dev cites Web Almanac data in which sites using third-party fonts rendered faster than self-hosting sites.
web-performance-sr10-09.explanation: web.dev says the Web Almanac saw faster renders with third-party fonts and that self-hosted fonts are much less likely to win without a CDN and HTTP/2.

web-performance-sr11-08.reason: ambiguous: 'updating a versioned asset' can mean publishing a new URL. The new wording pins the change to the same URL. web.dev: "the cached version is used until it's no longer fresh, as determined by max-age or expires", and versioning is done by "embedding a fingerprint of the file, or a version number, in its filename". (final: keep)
web-performance-sr11-08.statement: Replacing a file at the same URL on the server makes the browser refetch it while its cached copy is still fresh.
web-performance-sr11-08.explanation: The browser reuses a cached response until it is no longer fresh. web.dev puts a fingerprint or version in the file name, so changed content gets a new URL.
web-performance-sr11-08.misconception: Changing a file on the server invalidates a browser's fresh cached copy.

source.title: Prevent unnecessary network requests with the HTTP Cache

web-performance-sr12-06.reason: ambiguous: unclear which page holds the opener, and it made a two-page claim (it also carried the 'lets' tell). The new card states the source fact directly. web.dev: "a page with a non-null window.opener reference can't safely be put into bfcache, because that could break any pages attempting to access it." It also adds a web.dev-led false card to offset the web.dev-led-true tell. (final: fixed)
web-performance-sr12-06.statement: web.dev treats a page whose window.opener is non-null as a safe candidate for the bfcache.
web-performance-sr12-06.explanation: web.dev says a page with a non-null window.opener can't safely enter the bfcache, because pages trying to access it could break; rel="noopener" avoids creating the reference.
web-performance-sr12-06.misconception: Opener references between windows have no effect on bfcache eligibility.

web-performance-sr3-06.reason: tell: removes 'lets', which marked false statements (4 false to 1 true after the other edits). Fact and answer unchanged. (final: keep)
web-performance-sr3-06.statement: CSS upscaling makes an LCP image's reported area larger than the image's intrinsic area.
web-performance-sr3-06.explanation: LCP compensates for image upscaling, so CSS enlargement does not let the reported area exceed the image's intrinsic area.
web-performance-sr3-06.misconception: CSS enlargement increases measured image size beyond its intrinsic dimensions.

web-performance-sr10-10.reason: tell: removes 'lets' (a false-statement marker). Fact and answer unchanged. (final: fixed)
web-performance-sr10-10.statement: With unicode-range, the browser downloads the matching glyphs of a font as a partial file.
web-performance-sr10-10.explanation: unicode-range decides whether a font face is needed: MDN says if the page uses one character in the range, the whole font is downloaded. Byte savings come from separate subset files.
web-performance-sr10-10.misconception: The descriptor makes the browser download part of an individual font file.

web-performance-sr11-10.reason: tell: removes 'lets' (a false-statement marker). Fact and answer unchanged. (final: keep)
web-performance-sr11-10.statement: A client advertises the compression formats it accepts in a Content-Encoding request header.
web-performance-sr11-10.explanation: Content-Encoding identifies the coding applied to a representation. Accept-Encoding communicates the client's acceptable codings.
web-performance-sr11-10.misconception: Content-Encoding advertises the client's decoding preferences.

web-performance-sr3-07.reason: tell: breaks the 'X includes Y' false template (6 false to 4 true before the edits). Fact and answer unchanged. (final: keep)
web-performance-sr3-07.statement: LCP counts a text block's CSS padding as part of its candidate area.
web-performance-sr3-07.explanation: LCP sizes text using the bounds of its text nodes, excluding CSS padding, borders, and margins.
web-performance-sr3-07.misconception: LCP measures the decorated CSS box rather than the text area.

web-performance-sr4-03.reason: tell: breaks the 'X includes Y' false template. After this and sr3-07, 'includes' stands at 4 false (sr2-01, sr2-07, sr3-12, sr6-01) to 3 true. Fact and answer unchanged. (final: keep)
web-performance-sr4-03.statement: LCP resource load duration covers the wait to display an image after its download finishes.
web-performance-sr4-03.explanation: Waiting after the LCP resource finishes loading belongs to element render delay, not resource load duration.
web-performance-sr4-03.misconception: The resource loading phase continues until the browser paints the image.
